title: FUTA taxable wage base dashboard
subject: Federal revenue from raising the FUTA taxable wage base from $7,000 to $43,000 in 2026 and indexing it to the CPI-U, with the 0.6% net rate unchanged: the additional FUTA revenue by calendar year 2026-2035, adjusted (the headline, $251.1 billion over ten years) and unadjusted ($317.4 billion), counting the FUTA line only; the model's current-law FUTA revenue; and its fiscal-year validation against IRS collections for FY2024 and FY2025.
search_terms: raise FUTA taxable wage base CBO
unemployment insurance wage base revenue estimate
federal unemployment tax wage base $40,000 index wage growth
index the FUTA wage base inflation revenue

futa_base_43000_cpi_indexed.description: The dashboard's reform: the FUTA taxable wage base raised from $7,000 to $43,000 in 2026 and, from 2027, set to $43,000 times the prior calendar year's average CPI-U over the 2025 average, rounded to the nearest $100 ($53,200 in 2035); the 6.0% rate and the 5.4% maximum state credit (0.6% net) unchanged.

cbo_2016_option_futa_base_40000.description: CBO, Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2017 to 2026, Revenues Option 24, second alternative: the FUTA wage base raised to $40,000 in January 2017 and indexed to wage growth, the net FUTA rate cut from 0.6% to 0.167%; states must raise their own wage bases to at least $40,000.

cbo_2018_option_futa_base_40000.description: CBO, Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2019 to 2028, Revenues Option 23: the FUTA wage base raised to $40,000 in January 2019 and indexed to wage growth, the net FUTA rate cut from 0.6% to 0.167%; states must raise their own wage bases to at least $40,000.

futa_base_14000_unindexed.description: The Budget Lab's largest option: the FUTA wage base raised to $14,000 in 2026 and not indexed, at the 0.6% net rate.

futa_base_14000_chained_cpi_indexed.description: The Budget Lab: the FUTA wage base raised to $14,000 in 2026 and indexed to the chained CPI-U, at the 0.6% net rate.

futa_base_14000_wage_indexed.description: The Budget Lab: the FUTA wage base raised to $14,000 in 2026 and indexed to SSA's average wage index, at the 0.6% net rate.
